examples.en: How old is your younger sibling?
How old is the baby?
How old is your younger sibling now?
How old are you? Do you go to school?
How old is your nephew who lives in Seoul?
How old is that puppy over there?

explain: 나이는 ‘한 살, 스무 살’처럼 고유어 숫자로 말해요. 한국에서는 나이에 따라 말투와 호칭(언니, 형 등)이 달라져서 처음 만난 사람에게도 나이를 자주 물어요. 어른에게는 ‘연세가 어떻게 되세요?’, 비슷한 또래에게는 ‘나이가 어떻게 돼요?’라고 하면 공손해요.

phrases.en: How old are you?
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 편한 사이에서 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form, used with friends or close people.

phrases.en: What's your name? How old are you?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린아이에게 다정하게 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask a young child kindly.
phrases.en_equiv: how old are you (to a child)

phrases.en: How old is your child?
phrases.nuance_ko: '이세요'를 써서 조금 더 공손하게 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more respectful than the basic form.

dict_examples.en: How old is your daughter? — Five.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: How old is your dog?
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.ko: 형은 몇 살이에요? — 저보다 세 살 많아요.
dict_examples.en: How old is your older brother? — He's three years older than me.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: Ages use native numbers: 한 살, 스무 살. In Korea, age decides speech style and terms of address (언니, 형, etc.), so people often ask even on first meeting. To elders, say ‘연세가 어떻게 되세요?’; to people around your age, ‘나이가 어떻게 돼요?’ is polite.

examples.en: Hello? I'm Minsu. What's your name?
What is the name of the friend you just mentioned?

examples.ko: 저기 있는 저 가게 이름이 뭐예요?
examples.en: What is the name of that shop over there?
Excuse me, what is the name of this flower?
What is the name of your new puppy?
What is the name of this fruit in Korean?

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 가게, 꽃, 강아지처럼 이름이 있는 것에 모두 쓸 수 있어요. 어른께는 '성함이 어떻게 되세요?'라고 해야 더 공손해요. 친구에게는 '이름이 뭐야?'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 안녕, 나는 지수야. 너는 이름이 뭐야?
phrases.en: Hi, I'm Jisu. What's your name?
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 아랫사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for friends or people younger than you.

phrases.en: Excuse me, what is your name?
phrases.nuance_ko: '이름이 뭐예요?'보다 조금 부드럽고 공손하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds a little softer and more polite than the basic form.

phrases.example: 처음 만났으니까 이름 좀 알려 주세요.
phrases.en: We just met, so please tell me your name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문 대신 부탁하는 말로 이름을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asks for the name as a polite request instead of a question.

explain_en: You can use it not only for people but for anything with a name, such as shops, flowers, and puppies. To an elder, '성함이 어떻게 되세요?' is more polite. To a friend you say '이름이 뭐야?'.

examples.en: Hello, everyone! My name is Minsu.
My name is Michael. I'm from America.

examples.ko: 제 이름은 김하나예요. 하나라고 불러 주세요.
examples.en: My name is Kim Hana. Please call me Hana.

examples.ko: 제 이름은 아버지가 지어 주신 이름이에요.
examples.en: My name is a name my father gave me.

examples.ko: 제 이름은 길어서 친구들은 미아라고 불러요.
examples.en: My name is long, so my friends call me Mia.
My name is Sara. Nice to meet you.

explain: 자기소개의 첫 문장이에요. 이름이 모음으로 끝나면 '민수예요', 받침이 있으면 '마이클이에요'처럼 '이에요'를 써요. '저는 ...(이)라고 해요'라고도 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I am Minsu.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제 이름은'을 빼고 짧게 말하는 가장 쉬운 자기소개예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest, shortest way to introduce yourself, leaving out the word for 'my name'.

phrases.en: I'm called Michael.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 조금 더 부드럽고 자연스럽게 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly softer, more natural way of introducing your name.

phrases.en: To a friend, you say 'My name is Minsu.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 어린 사람에게 쓰는 반말이라서 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for friends or younger people, so you don't use it with elders.

explain_en: This is the first sentence of a self-introduction. If the name ends in a vowel, use '예요', as in '민수예요'; if it ends in a consonant, use '이에요', as in '마이클이에요'. You can also say '저는 ...(이)라고 해요'.

examples.en: Where are you from, teacher?
Where is that friend from?

examples.ko: 처음 뵌 선생님은 어느 나라 사람이에요?
examples.en: Which country is the teacher I just met from?

examples.ko: 새로 온 학생은 어느 나라 사람이에요?
examples.en: Which country is the new student from?
Which country is that singer from?
Excuse me, which country are you from?

explain: 국적을 묻는 말이고, 대답은 '저는 미국 사람이에요'나 '미국에서 왔어요'라고 해요. 어른에게는 '어느 나라 분이세요?'라고 높여요. 여러 나라 중에서 고르는 느낌이라 '무슨 나라'가 아니라 '어느 나라'를 써요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, which country are you from?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이나 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰는 높임말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form, for elders or people you've just met.

phrases.en: To a friend, you ask 'Which country are you from?'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 어린 사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used between friends or with younger people.

phrases.en: Minsu, which country did you come from?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에서 왔는지 묻는 느낌이라 조금 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asks where you came from rather than what your nationality is, so it sounds a bit gentler.
phrases.en_equiv: which country did you come from?

dict_examples.ko: 어느 나라 사람이에요? — 저는 호주 사람이에요.
dict_examples.en: Where are you from? — I'm Australian.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.en: Which country is that singer from?
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.ko: 새로 온 학생은 어느 나라 사람이에요? — 몽골 사람이에요.
dict_examples.en: Where is the new student from? — Mongolia.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: It asks about nationality, and answers are '저는 미국 사람이에요' or '미국에서 왔어요'. To an elder, honor it as '어느 나라 분이세요?'. It uses '어느' instead of '무슨' because you choose among many countries.

examples.en: Hello? What's your job? I'm a teacher.
What is Minsu's older brother's job?
What are Minsu's parents' jobs?
Excuse me, what is your job?

examples.ko: 한국에서 요즘 인기 있는 직업이 뭐예요?
examples.en: What are popular jobs in Korea these days?
What does the newcomer do for a living?

explain: 직업을 묻는 기본 표현이지만 조금 직접적으로 들릴 수 있어요. 처음 만난 사람에게는 '무슨 일을 하세요?'가 더 부드러워요. 대답은 '저는 선생님이에요', '회사원이에요'처럼 해요.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you. What do you do for work?
phrases.nuance_ko: '직업이 뭐예요?'보다 부드러워서 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than the headword, so it suits people you've just met.
phrases.en_equiv: what do you do for work?

phrases.en: To a friend, you ask 'What's your job?'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 어린 사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used with friends or younger people.

phrases.en: My job is teacher. (I'm a teacher.)
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문에 대답할 때 쓰는 말로, 직업을 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to answer the question and state your job clearly.

explain_en: This is the basic way to ask about someone's job, but it can sound a bit direct. To someone you just met, '무슨 일을 하세요?' is softer. Answers look like '저는 선생님이에요' or '회사원이에요'.

examples.en: How's the weather today?
How's the weather in Seoul?

examples.ko: 내일 부산에 가는데 거기 날씨가 어때요?
examples.en: I'm going to Busan tomorrow. How is the weather there?

examples.ko: 여보세요, 엄마! 거기 요즘 날씨가 어때요?
examples.en: Hello, Mom! How is the weather there these days?

examples.ko: 비가 많이 온다고 들었는데 제주도는 날씨가 어때요?
examples.en: I heard it rains a lot. How is the weather in Jeju?

examples.ko: 주말에 소풍을 가고 싶은데 그날 날씨가 어때요?
examples.en: I want to go on a picnic this weekend. How is the weather that day?

explain: 장소나 때를 앞에 붙여서 '서울은 날씨가 어때요?', '내일 날씨가 어때요?'처럼 물어요. 대답은 '맑아요', '더워요', '비가 와요'처럼 날씨 상태로 해요. 친구끼리는 '날씨 어때?'라고 짧게 말해요.

phrases.en: To a friend, you ask 'How's the weather there?'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게 쓰는 짧은 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short, casual form for friends and family.

phrases.en: How's the weather today? Do I need an umbrella?
phrases.nuance_ko: '오늘'을 붙여서 지금 날씨를 물을 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the word for 'today' makes it a question about the current weather.

phrases.en: The weather is nice today. Let's go for a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문에 대한 대답으로 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to answer the question.

dict_examples.en: How's the weather? — Clear and warm.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.ko: 주말에 날씨가 어때요? 등산을 가고 싶어요.
dict_examples.en: How's the weather this weekend? I want to go hiking.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

dict_examples.ko: 거기는 지금 날씨가 어때요? — 비가 많이 와요.
dict_examples.en: How's the weather there now? — It's raining a lot.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: Put a place or a time before it, as in '서울은 날씨가 어때요?' or '내일 날씨가 어때요?'. You answer with the weather itself, such as '맑아요', '더워요' or '비가 와요'. Between friends people shorten it to '날씨 어때?'.

examples.ko: 지금 뭐 하세요? 시간 있으면 같이 먹어요.
examples.en: What are you doing now? If you have time, let's eat together.
What do you usually do on weekends?
Teacher, what do you do after work?

examples.ko: 여보세요? 아버지, 지금 집에서 뭐 하세요?
examples.en: Hello? Dad, what are you doing at home now?

examples.ko: 거기서 혼자 뭐 하세요? 같이 가요.
examples.en: What are you doing there alone? Let's go together.
Are you busy these days? What will you do during vacation?

explain: '하세요'는 높임말이라서 선생님이나 처음 만난 사람에게 써요. 친구에게는 '뭐 해요?'나 '뭐 해?'라고 말해요. 직업을 물을 때는 '무슨 일 하세요?'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 지금 뭐 해요? 같이 점심 먹어요.
phrases.en: What are you doing now? Let's have lunch together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뭐 하세요?'보다 편하게 묻는 말로, 친구나 아는 사이에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More relaxed than the headword, for friends or people you know.

phrases.en: To a friend, you ask 'What are you doing now?'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 어린 사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used with friends or younger people.

phrases.example: 처음 만났을 때 '무슨 일 하세요?'라고 물어요.
phrases.en: When meeting for the first time, you ask 'What do you do for work?'
phrases.nuance_ko: '뭐 하세요?'는 지금 하는 일도 묻지만, 이 말은 직업을 묻는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The headword can ask what someone is doing right now, but this one asks about their job.
phrases.en_equiv: what do you do for work?

explain_en: '하세요' is the honorific form, so use it with teachers or people you have just met. With friends, say '뭐 해요?' or '뭐 해?'. To ask about someone's job, say '무슨 일 하세요?'.

en: polite way to ask for information (e.g. name, age)

examples.en: Excuse me, may I ask your name?
What is today's date?
Excuse me, may I ask how old your grandmother is?
Sorry, but what is your contact number, sir?

examples.ko: 회사 위치가 어떻게 되는지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me where your company is located.

examples.ko: 우리 집 주소가 어떻게 되는지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you know what our home address is?

explain: 이름, 나이, 연락처, 주소를 높여서 물을 때 '뭐예요?' 대신 써요. '어떻게 해요?'는 '내가 무엇을 해야 해요?'라는 다른 뜻이니까 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: May I ask what your name is?
phrases.nuance_ko: '어떻게 되세요?'보다 조금 더 정중해서 가게나 전화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more polite than the basic form, often used in shops and on the phone.

phrases.en: Excuse me, may I ask how old you are?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른께 나이를 높여서 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask an older person's age respectfully.

phrases.en: Sorry, but what is your phone number?
phrases.nuance_ko: 연락처나 주소도 같은 틀로 정중하게 물을 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same pattern works for politely asking contact details or an address.

explain_en: Use it to ask politely for a name, age, contact number or address, instead of the blunter '뭐예요?'. Don't confuse it with '어떻게 해요?', which means 'What should I do?'.

examples.en: When you get older, time goes by fast.
The older I get, the more I worry about my health.
My younger sibling still likes toys even when older.

examples.ko: 올해 한 살 더 나이를 먹었어요.
examples.en: I got a year older this year.

examples.ko: 나이를 먹으니까 예전처럼 밤을 새우기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Now that I'm older, I can't stay up all night like I used to.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지도 나이를 먹어서 많이 느려졌어요.
examples.en: Our puppy has gotten older and has become much slower.

explain: '나이를 먹다'는 나이가 많아진다는 뜻으로, 조금 아쉬운 느낌이 있을 때 자주 써요. 어른에게는 '나이를 드시다'라고 높여요. '나이가 들다'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: As you get older, your eyesight gets worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나이를 먹다'와 비슷하고 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, and sounds a little gentler.

phrases.en: Even though Grandfather is getting older, he is healthy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른의 나이를 말할 때 높여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form used for elders.

phrases.en: The older I get, the more precious my friends are.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ수록'은 나이가 많아지는 것에 따라 달라지는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This pattern describes something that changes as age increases.

explain_en: '나이를 먹다' means getting older and is often used with a slightly wistful feeling. For an elder you honor it as '나이를 드시다'. '나이가 들다' is a similar expression.

examples.en: Excuse me, what month and day is your birthday?
Wait a moment, what is today's date?

examples.ko: 한국에 도착하는 날이 몇 월 며칠이에요?
examples.en: What date do you arrive in Korea?
Do you know what date the exam is?

examples.ko: 달력을 보고 몇 월 며칠인지 확인했어요.
examples.en: I looked at the calendar and checked the date.
What date was your parents' wedding anniversary?

explain: 날짜를 묻는 가장 기본적인 말이에요. 대답은 '3월 5일이에요'처럼 숫자로 해요. 요일은 '무슨 요일이에요?'라고 따로 물어요. '며칠'은 '몇 일'이라고 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Wait, what's the date today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 월은 알고 날짜만 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you know the month and only want the day.

phrases.en: What month is it now?
phrases.nuance_ko: 달만 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asks only for the month.

phrases.en: What day of the week is it tomorrow?
phrases.nuance_ko: 날짜 대신 요일을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asks for the day of the week instead of the date.
phrases.en_equiv: What day of the week is it?

explain_en: This is the most basic way to ask for a date. The answer uses numbers, as in '3월 5일이에요'. The weekday is asked separately with '무슨 요일이에요?'. '며칠' is never written as '몇 일'.

examples.en: What's your friend's name?
This isn't my name.
What's your name? — I'm Haruka.
I write my name on the paper.
This café has a pretty name.

explain: 어른에게는 '이름' 대신 '성함'을 써요: '성함이 어떻게 되세요?' 그리고 한국어는 성(김, 이, 박)이 먼저, 이름이 뒤예요. 이름만 부르는 건 친한 사이에서만 해요.

phrases.en: to live up to one's name/reputation
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 좋을 때 칭찬
phrases.nuance_en: a compliment when something is as good as expected
phrases.en_equiv: to live up to one's name/reputation

phrases.example: 이름도 성도 모르는 사람이 돈을 빌려 달래요.
phrases.en: to not know someone at all
phrases.nuance_ko: 전혀 모르는 사람이라는 것을 강조
phrases.nuance_en: stresses that you don't know the person at all
phrases.en_equiv: to not know someone at all

explain_en: For elders, use the honorific 성함 instead of 이름: 성함이 어떻게 되세요? ('May I ask your name?'). Korean names put the family name (Kim, Lee, Park) first. Calling someone by given name alone is only for close relationships.

dis.h: Everyday word for names, including people

p.n: 명칭 is more formal and used only for things or organizations.

explain_en: 끝나다 is for something that ends by itself (일이 끝나요). When a person finishes something, use 끝내다 (일을 끝내요). The particle changes from 이/가 to 을/를.

dis.h: general: something comes to an end

p.n: 종료되다 sounds formal, like an official announcement.

explain_en: In speech people say 전에 more often. 이전 shows up more in notices and writing. Its opposite is 이후.

dis.h: formal; earlier than a point, previous

p.n: Both mean 'before'. 전 is more casual, and 이전 sounds more formal.
